plan: In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. This is because you pay the second-highest bid if you win, not your own bid, so overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth, while underbidding risks losing profitable auctions. With my value at $30, I should bid exactly $30 to maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price (Vickrey) auction with 3 bidders and independent private values. In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what others do - it maximizes expected profit. Bidding higher risks overpaying if I win; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Since my value is $28, I should bid exactly $28 to ensure optimal outcomes in both winning and losing scenarios.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors or their strategies. This is because you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid, so overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth, while underbidding risks losing auctions you could have profitably won. Since my value is $22, I should bid exactly $22 to maximize expected profit.
